reflection_text.2:
The model is per-haplotype random false-negative loss of derived alleles with retention probability q<1 independent across samples, followed by reference imputation. A true ancestral copy is always seen as reference; a true derived copy is seen as derived with prob q and is turned to reference otherwise.
For a true haploid derived frequency p>0

E[p_obs]=p q < p

E[H_obs]=2 p q(1-p q) < 2p(1-p)=H_true

for every 0<p<1, 0<q<1. So π = E_s[2p_s(1-p_s)] is systematically deflated by the frequency attenuation p→p q. The attenuation is constant in p and does not vanish with n. This is the classic reference-imputation downward bias for allele-frequency based statistics.

Watterson depends only on presence/absence on the fixed VCF union of SNVs. By construction no site is completely missing in the original panel. For a site with k=2 n p true derived copies

Pr{p_obs=0|k}= (1-q)^k , Pr{site seen segregating}=1-(1-q)^k.

With fixed p>0, k→∞ as n→∞ so Pr{site seen}→1. Under the infinite-sites spectrum

E[S_obs]= Σ θ/k [1-(1-q)^k] = θ a_n - θ Σ (1-q)^k/k
       = θ a_n - θ[-ln q].

The loss of segregating sites is O(1) while E[S_true]=θ a_n∼θ log n diverges. Hence
E[S_obs]/E[S_true]=1 - [-ln q]/a_n →1 and
θ_W,obs = S_obs/a_n → S_true/a_n in the n→∞ limit on the ascertained SNV set.

Thus in the arbitrarily large-n limit stated, the count of segregating sites, and hence Watterson’s θ_W on the ascertained set, is asymptotically recovered, the residual finite-n loss being O(1/a_n). The frequency information on which π is based is permanently attenuated.

Colleague split persists:
B camp 10,11,12,2,3,4,6,8: π persistently downward biased, θ_W asymptotically unbiased on the ascertained set.
A/C camp 1,7,13,14,9,5: emphasize neutral spectrum tail replenishment, singletons/doubletons keep entering as n grows, finite correction θ[-ln q] never negligible relative to a_n∼ln n, so θ_W remains detectably downward biased in any realistic, even arbitrarily large, panel; and both estimators are technically downward biased in any finite sample.

Unresolved/important nuance: interpretation of “arbitrarily large” as formal n→∞ limit vs practical finite panel. The O(1/a_n) rare-allele loss for θ_W vanishes in the formal limit but is O(1/ln n) in practice. Ascertainment upward bias to SNVs is common to both statistics and is not the bias introduced by filtering+reference imputation.

Current best belief remains B: only π is biased in the large-n limit; Watterson’s θ is asymptotically unbiased for the ascertained SNV set under random independent loss + reference imputation, with the usual O(1/a_n) finite-sample downward bias that vanishes as n→∞. The persistent, non-vanishing bias is in π. If the question is read as strictly finite-sample, both estimators are technically downward biased, which is the C argument.
reflection_text.3:
The data generating process is a fixed ascertained union of SNVs with no site completely missing in the original VCF. Per haplotype a true derived allele is retained with probability q<1 and otherwise deleted; deleted genotypes are imputed to reference. Imputation is one-way loss: P(obs derived|true derived)=q, P(obs derived|true ancestral)=0.

For a site with true haplotypic derived frequency p>0
 E[p_obs]=q p < p
 E[H_obs]=2 p_obs(1-p_obs)=2 q p(1-q p) < 2 p(1-p)=H_true
for every 0<p<1, 0<q<1. Hence site heterozygosity and mean pairwise difference are attenuated by frequency thinning. Averaged over sites π_obs = E[2p_obs(1-p_obs)] < E[2p(1-p)] = π_true and the attenuation is a constant factor in p, it does not vanish with n.

Presence/absence. A truly segregating site with k=2np true derived copies is seen as monomorphic after imputation iff all k copies are deleted.
Pr[p_obs=0|k]=(1-q)^k
Pr[site seen segregating|k]=1-(1-q)^k
For fixed p>0, k→∞ as n→∞, so Pr[seen]→1. On the ascertained set
E[S_obs]=∑i[1-(1-q)^{k_i}] = θ a_n - θ∑_{k≥1}(1-q)^k/k = θ a_n - θ[-log q]
The loss of segregating sites is O(1), finite, whereas E[S_true]=θ a_n ∼ θ log n diverges. Hence E[S_obs]/E[S_true]→1 and
θ_W,obs = S_obs/a_n → S_true/a_n
in the n→∞ limit on the ascertained SNV set. The O(1) rare-allele loss is O(1/a_n).

The classic false-negative / reference-imputation asymmetry therefore holds: S is robust to random copy loss, π is sensitive to allele-frequency attenuation. The usual ascertainment bias to the SNV set is common to both statistics and is not the bias introduced here.

Disagreement in round 2:
* B camp 10,11,12,2,3,4,6,8: only π persistently downward biased, θ_W asymptotically unbiased on the ascertained set. Math above.
* A/C camp 1,7,13,14,5,9: neutral spectrum continually feeds new ultra-rare variants as n grows; the finite correction θ[-ln q] is continually replenished, a_n∼ln n grows slowly, so a non-vanishing fractional bias in θ_W remains in any realistic “arbitrarily large” panel. Some in this camp also claim π is largely cancelled after imputation, favoring A; others claim both are down-biased, favoring C.
* Colleague 1 earlier claimed π unbiased, which is inconsistent with E[H_obs]<H_true.
* Unresolved nuance: definition of bias relative to true genome-wide diversity vs bias relative to the ascertained SNV set, and whether “arbitrarily large” is taken as genuine limit n→∞, in which case fractional loss of S→0, or as very large but finite where θ_W bias is O(1/a_n) and practically detectable.

Current best read remains B in the strict n→∞ limit stated in the problem: π is persistently downward biased by one-way reference imputation, Watterson’s θ is asymptotically recovered on the fixed ascertained SNV union, with a finite-sample O(1/a_n) downward bias in θ_W that vanishes as a_n→∞. The A/C dissent is essentially the finite-sample O(1/log n) rare-allele loss argument.

9.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: Colleague 13 and 9 are right that the neutral spectrum’s continual renewal of singletons and doubletons prevents the finite loss term θ[–ln q] from being amortized away even as n grows arbitrarily large. Because each new ultra-rare variant enters with a retention probability that remains bounded away from 1, the expected deficit in realized segregating sites stays order-1 relative to the slowly growing a_n ∼ ln(2n). This produces a persistent fractional downward bias in observed S and therefore in θ_W on the ascertained set. At the same time the identical one-way reference imputation multiplies every retained frequency by q, shrinking every 2p(1–p) term and thereby depressing π uniformly across the union. The two biases are additive rather than mutually exclusive: tail loss directly reduces the numerator of Watterson’s estimator while frequency attenuation reduces the heterozygosity contributions that enter π. The fact that ascertainment itself occurs after per-sample filtering only compounds the problem, since any singleton whose last derived copy is deleted never enters the VCF union at all. Consequently both statistics remain systematically underestimated under the stated procedure, even in the arbitrarily-large-n regime. This favors C.

14.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: Colleague 1 and 14 have the sharper reading here. Even in the arbitrarily large-n regime the neutral spectrum is not a static ascertained union; new singletons and doubletons continue to enter at rate θ/k, each carrying a per-haplotype retention probability bounded away from 1. The resulting deficit θ[−ln q] therefore remains a fixed subtraction from S while a_n grows only logarithmically, so the relative downward shift in θ_W stays O(1/a_n) and is still appreciable for any realistically finite though “arbitrarily large” human panel. In contrast, once a site survives filtering the subsequent reference imputation attenuates every retained frequency by the same factor q; when these attenuated frequencies are averaged across all pairs the net effect on π largely cancels because every haplotype pair is weighted equally. The net result is that the tail loss permanently depresses the segregating-site count used by Watterson’s estimator while the pairwise averaging that defines π is effectively unbiased on the imputed sequences. That spectrum-weighted distinction favors A over the pure-asymptotic recovery claimed for θ_W.

7.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: Colleague 5’s observation about the continually refreshed ultra-rare tail is exactly the point that keeps the O(1/a_n) deficit from disappearing in any practical panel, even one labeled “arbitrarily large.” The neutral spectrum supplies new singletons and doubletons at rate θ/k, each with retention probability bounded well below 1; because a_n grows only logarithmically, that constant loss term θ[–ln q] remains a non-negligible fraction of realized S. Consequently the downward bias in θ_W stays detectable long after every fixed-p site has been recovered with probability approaching 1. At the same time the reference-imputation step multiplies every surviving frequency by q, which depresses the heterozygosity terms that enter π. The two effects are not mutually exclusive: the tail loss hits the segregating-site count while frequency attenuation hits the pairwise average, so both statistics are pulled downward on the post-filter ascertained set. That spectrum-weighted view favors A (or at minimum C) over the clean asymptotic separation claimed for θ_W.

1.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: Colleague 1 and 14 are correct that the continuing arrival of new singletons and doubletons under the neutral spectrum keeps a fixed downward correction θ[–ln q] alive relative to the slowly growing a_n ∼ ln(2n), so the realized S on any filtered VCF is thinned before imputation even occurs. Because every newly arising ultra-rare variant still faces a non-negligible per-copy loss probability q that does not shrink with panel size, the fractional deficit in segregating sites remains detectable for any realistically attainable (even if “arbitrarily large”) human phased cohort; the O(1/a_n) term therefore never becomes negligible in practice and systematically depresses Watterson’s estimator. In contrast, once the surviving sites are completed by reference imputation the pairwise averaging that defines π experiences frequency attenuation that largely cancels across the now-complete sequences, because every pair is weighted equally and the one-way loss p → p q is applied uniformly. This spectrum-weighted view therefore isolates the persistent bias to the segregating-site count alone, favoring A over the asymptotic-recovery arguments that implicitly treat the tail as static rather than continually refreshed. At the same time, reference imputation multiplies every retained frequency by q, uniformly shrinking every 2p(1–p) term that feeds π; the resulting attenuation is therefore additive rather than mutually exclusive. The B camp’s clean asymptotic recovery for θ_W tacitly assumes a static list of sites whose minimum k diverges uniformly—an assumption the infinite-sites model itself violates.

For a site with true haploid derived frequency p>0 on the fixed VCF union

E[pobs|p]=p q < p

and

E[2pobs(1-pobs)|p]=2pq(1-pq) < 2p(1-p).

Hence for every site

E[Hobs] < Htrue

and with mean pairwise differences

πobs = Es[2p s,obs(1-p s,obs)]

πobs is systematically deflated by the frequency thinning p→pq. The
attenuation is genotype dependent and does not vanish with n. Ascertainment
to the SNV union is common to both statistics.

Watterson uses only presence/absence. On the fixed union a site is truly
segregating, p>0. With k_n=2np true derived copies

Pr{pobs=0|k_n}=f^{k_n}=(1-q)^{k_n},
Pr{site seen segregating|k_n}=1-(1-q)^{k_n}.

For any fixed p>0, k_n→∞ as n→∞ and (1-q)^{k_n}→0. On the infinite sites
spectrum

E[Sobs]=∑_{k≥1} θ/k [1-(1-q)^k]=θ a_n - θ∑_{k≥1}(1-q)^k/k
      =θ a_n - θ[-ln q],

θW,obs=Sobs/a_n → Strue/a_n

in probability on the ascertained SNV set. The O(1/a_n) rare-allele loss
vanishes in the n→∞ limit.

That is the classic false-negative / reference-imputation asymmetry:
S, and therefore Watterson’s θW on the ascertained set, is robust to random

The core mechanism is per-haplotype random false negative with retention probability q<1 then one-way reference imputation. True ancestral is always seen as reference; true derived is seen as derived with prob q and turned to reference with prob 1-q.

For a site with true haploid derived frequency p>0,
E[p_obs]=p q < p.
E[H_obs]=2 p q(1-p q) < 2p(1-p)=H_true,
E[Y_i xor Y_j]=2 p q -2 p² q² <2p-2p².
Hence mean pairwise difference and π = L⁻¹ Σ 2p_s(1-p_s) is systematically deflated by frequency attenuation p→p q. The bias is constant in n and does not vanish with sample size; imputation is one-way loss.

Segregation is presence/absence. With k=2 n p true derived copies,
Pr[site observed monomorphic]=(1-q)^k, Pr[segregating]=1-(1-q)^k.
For fixed p>0, k→∞ as n→∞, so Pr→1. On the fixed ascertained SNV union,
E[S_obs]= Σ_i[1-(1-q)^{k_i}] = θ a_n - θ Σ_k (1-q)^k/k.
Σ_k (1-q)^k/k = -log q <∞ is O(1), while E[S_true]=θ a_n ∼θ log n diverges. Hence
E[S_obs]/E[S_true]=1 - O(1/a_n)→1,
and S_obs → S_true in probability on the ascertained set. Therefore θ_W = S_obs/a_n is asymptotically unbiased for diversity defined on the ascertained set as n→∞; the finite-sample loss is θ[-log q]/a_n = O(1/log n) vanishing in the limit.

B camp 10,11,12,2,3,4,6,8: only π persistently biased, θ_W asymptotically unbiased on the fixed VCF union in the n→∞ limit. They stress E[p_obs]=p q, E[H_obs]<H_true permanently, while Pr[site seen]=1-(1-q)^k→1 for any fixed p>0, so S loss is the finite constant θ[-log q] vs diverging a_n.

Consequently both statistics remain systematically underestimated, which favors C over the clean asymptotic separation claimed for θ_W.

7.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: Colleague 5’s question about whether the dynamic tail truly lets the logarithmic correction vanish is exactly the right one to press here. so site heterozygosity and mean pairwise differences are permanently attenuated by the p→p q thinning. Hence π_obs = E_s[2 p_s,obs(1-p_s,obs)] is systematically downward biased and the bias does not vanish with n, up to the SNV ascertainment common to both statistics.

Watterson depends on presence/absence on the fixed VCF union. On the fixed union a site with k_n=2 n p true derived copies is observed monomorphic after imputation iff all copies are deleted:

Pr{p_obs=0|k_n}=(1-q)^{k_n},  Pr{site seen|k_n}=1-(1-q)^{k_n}.

For any fixed p>0, k_n→∞ as n→∞ and Pr{seen}→1. On the infinite-sites spectrum

E[S_obs]=∑_i[1-(1-q)^{k_i}] = θ a_n - θ∑_{k≥1}(1-q)^k/k = θ a_n - θ[-ln q],
E[S_true]=θ a_n ∼ θ ln n.

The loss of segregating sites is the finite O(1) term θ[-ln q] whereas S_true diverges. Hence
E[S_obs]/a_n = θ[1-(-ln q)/a_n] → θ ,   θ_W,obs=S_obs/a_n → S_true/a_n
on the ascertained SNV set. The fractional loss is O(1/a_n)→0. This is the classic false-negative / reference-imputation asymmetry: S and therefore Watterson’s θ_W on the ascertained set is robust to random independent copy loss, π is not.

Current round majority 10,11,12,2,3,4,6,8 restate this B argument with E[p_obs]=p q, E[H_obs]=2pq(1-pq) attenuation and the 1-(1-q)^{k_n} presence/absence recovery and the θ a_n - θ[-ln q] calculation.

Colleagues 1,13,14,7,9 argue the neutral 1/k spectrum continually replenishes ultra-rare variants, so the finite deficit θ[-ln q] is continually refreshed and the O(1/a_n) fractional downward shift in θ_W remains detectable for any realistically attainable, even “arbitrarily large”, human panel. 1 and 14 additionally claim pairwise averaging cancels the π attenuation, which is inconsistent with the one-way loss p→p q. The A claim that only θ_W is biased and π is essentially unbiased is mathematically incorrect under the stated one-way imputation.

Colleague 13/14 also press ascertainment timing: per-sample quality filtering before the VCF union is formed means any singleton/doubleton whose last derived copy is dropped never appears in the ascertained set at all; the realized site list is already thinned by the same q^k factor. That would make the θ[-ln q] deficit subtract from an already reduced numerator and keep both statistics down-biased. Colleague 5/9 similarly argue both S and π are systematically underestimated in practice.

Unresolved tension is finite-sample vs formal n→∞. In a strictly finite sample both statistics are technically down-biased, the Watterson bias being O(1/a_n) ~ θ[-ln q]/ln n and the π bias being O(1) in q. With the arbitrarily large n stated in the question the formal limit is asymptotic recovery of θ_W on the fixed ascertained union while π remains permanently attenuated. The practical objection is that a_n grows only logarithmically, so the θ[-ln q]/a_n term may remain non-negligible for human-scale panels, motivating the A/C position. Under the strict formal limit as phrased, the persistent bias is confined to π, i.e. B.
